topIssues.title: [PCD Milestone 4] Commit the prepare artifacts
topIssues.author: 0xiamflux
topIssues.body:
## Context
Permissionless deployment pipelines need `genesis.json`, `rollup.json`, and `depsets.json` available in the devnet repo for the out-of-band computation of the prestate hash and its later verification. After `prepare` produces those artifacts,
they need to be committed to the devnet repo.

netchef opens a PR to the devnet repo carrying the artifacts, tagged with `#netchef-skip-workflows` so the commit does not re-trigger CI's workflow dispatch.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Given the `op-deployer prepare` output, `CreateNetwork` opens a PR to the devnet repo containing all the artifacts the prestate computation needs.
- [ ] The PR commit carries `#netchef-skip-workflows`, and on merge CI is observed not to dispatch a second workflow.
- [ ] The PR is opened on the permissionless path only, permissioned only deployments use the existing flow.

- `/op-stack/interop/interop` (59 lines): thin intro whose substance the interop hub (`/op-stack/interop`) and the explainer (`/op-stack/interop/explainer`) already cover. topPRs.title: refactor: share jovian base fee calculation
topPRs.author: cliff0412
topPRs.body:
## Summary

  - Move OP Jovian next-block base fee calculation into `op-alloy-consensus`
  - Reuse the shared helper from Kona executor and op-reth chainspec
  - Add direct tests for Jovian DA-footprint gas selection and minimum base fee clamping

  ## Details

  Jovian base fee calculation extends normal EIP-1559 behavior by:

  - using `max(parent.gas_used, parent.blob_gas_used.unwrap_or_default())`
  - clamping the result to the encoded `min_base_fee`

  This logic existed separately in Kona executor and op-reth chainspec. This PR centralizes it in `op-alloy-consensus`, next to the existing Jovian extra-data encode/decode helpers.

topPRs.title: op-node: reset non-canonical pending safe head
topPRs.author: jelias2
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Clear reported pending-safe state when derivation resets.
- Seed reported pending-safe state from local-safe when engine reset completes.
- When a pending-safe parent is missing by hash, compare the canonical block at the same height and return a reset error on a definitive hash mismatch.
- Remove the earlier supernode VN restart workaround.

## Root cause

PendingSafeL2 is not persisted in SafeDB. It is runtime engine-controller state, while the sync-status tracker separately mirrors it for RPC consumers.

Two generic op-node behaviors combined during the reorg recovery:

1. Reset events did not clear or reseed StatusTracker.PendingSafeL2, so optimism_syncStatus could report an orphaned head after engine reset.
2. PreparePayloadAttributes classified a missing parent hash as temporary even when the EL had a different canonical block at the same number. Derivation retried instead of resetting.

The canonical by-number comparison makes the reset decision only when the EL proves the old hash is non-canonical. If that comparison cannot be completed, the existing temporary-error behavior remains.

## Non-goals

This does not repair supernode logsDB/accepted-state divergence, proxyd freshness or monotonicity policy, or Reth ExEx WAL consistency.

## Tests

- go test ./op-node/rollup/status ./op-node/rollup/derive -run 'TestResetEventClearsPendingSafe|TestEngineResetConfirmedSetsPendingSafeToLocalSafe|TestPreparePayloadAttributes/non-canonical' -count=1
- go test ./op-node/rollup/... -count=1
- go test ./op-node/... -count=1

All passed.

topPRs.title: docs: add Get Started home tab as the docs landing experience
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784834359611159?thread_ts=1784834359.611159&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

Closes [ethereum-optimism/solutions#987](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/issues/987). Note for the merger: cross-repo `Closes` does not auto-fire, so the closure needs a manual check on merge. That issue was in fact already auto-closed on 2026-07-23 when the IA plan landed in the solutions repo; this PR is the change that actually delivers what it asks for, so on merge please just confirm the closure stands. Tracking issue for this slice: [ethereum-optimism/solutions#1040](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/issues/1040).

Iteration-2 IA modernization, slice 1 of 9 (`projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md` in the solutions repo). **This PR holds the program's serialized docs.json slot**: at most one PR touching docs.json nav or redirects is in flight at a time across both program lanes, and this is it (the previous holder, the D6 merge, landed as #22003).

## Before / After

**Before:** docs.optimism.io lands visitors inside the Chain Operators tab. The site root (`index`, the persona router) is nav-homed in `Chain Operators > Quickstart`, and Chain Operators is the first tab, so every visitor gets the chain-operator sidebar and tab highlight. The `ai-docs` page and all six `use-cases/*` solution guides share that same wrong home.

**After:** a new **Get Started** tab, first in the tab bar, owns the site root with audience routing and the five solution guides:

- Group "Get started": `index` (persona router), `ai-docs`, `chain-operators/quickstart`
- Group "Use cases": `use-cases/index` plus `tune-batcher-costs`, `run-a-fault-proof-challenger`, `implement-a-custom-deposit-flow`, `launch-a-chain-with-fault-proofs-and-ha-sequencing`, `choose-your-node-stack`

The router cards on `index.mdx` already list app developers first (per the Q1 resolution); no content edit was needed, and none was made.

## How

- **Nav-only, one file:** `docs/public-docs/docs.json`, +8/-3 lines. Zero content files changed, zero URL changes, zero redirects (622 redirect entries before and after).
- **Pure insertion:** Get Started is inserted at position 1; the other 7 tabs keep their exact current relative order (Q1 resolution: no reordering).
- **Exact removal:** the Quickstart group (3 entries) and Use cases group (6 entries) are removed from Chain Operators (82 -> 73 entries); nothing else in that tab changes.
- **Invariant:** 408 unique nav entries before and after, zero nav duplicates. (The plan's acceptance text says 411 because it was written at the pre-D6 audit tip; D6 (#22003) merged 3 pages away before this slice ran. The criterion's substance, count unchanged and no duplicates, holds.)
- `choose-your-node-stack` stays with the Use cases group per the plan ("stays with the Use cases group for now"; revisit when IA slice 3 lands). Contribute does not move here; the Q4 ruling (Contribute to the bottom of the Get Started tab) is slice 2's scope.

**Accepted interim state (not a regression):** the Chain Operators tab now opens on the first page of its Guides group (`chain-operators/guides/configuration/getting-started`) until IA slice 4 gives it a tab-level index page. The plan sanctions this explicitly; it is still strictly better than before, when that tab opened on the site root.

## Verification (independent adversarial pass)

Scripted semantic JSON diff of `docs.json` between develop `0f0aba35` and this branch, 25 checks, all passing:

- Get Started inserted at position 1; the other 7 tabs in identical relative order; the 6 tabs other than Chain Operators byte-identical.
- Get Started holds exactly the plan's 9 entries in exactly the plan's 2 groups and order; all 9 resolve to existing page files on disk.
- Chain Operators removals are exactly those 9 entries (groups Quickstart and Use cases); remaining 73 entries keep their order; no `index`, `ai-docs`, or `use-cases/*` entry survives there.
- With the two verified tabs factored out, the rest of the file is semantically identical: redirects (622, untouched), theme, colors, footer, everything.
- 408 unique nav entries before and after; identical page set (zero URL changes, so the zero-redirect claim is sound).
- `index` is the first tab's first entry, which is what re-homes the site root's tab highlight (this is the same pattern the plan verified against a peer Mintlify site: root homed inside a small first Get Started tab).
- Lints, all from `docs/public-docs`: `pnpm lint:nav` OK (409 pages on disk, 408 distinct nav entries, 1 allowlisted orphan); `pnpm lint:redirects` OK (622 redirects, 442 files scanned, 17 grandfathered violations, unchanged from develop); `node scripts/lint-link-policy.mjs --baseline scripts/lint-link-policy.baseline.json --specs-src <local specs checkout>` 0 findings, clean. Zero baseline growth on all three.
- No other open program branch touches docs.json (D8 and the OPE slices are content-only, verified by diff).

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] **Open the Mintlify preview root URL and confirm it lands on the Get Started tab with the correct tab highlight** (preview deployments are proxy-blocked for the agent sessions, so this render check is on you), and that the tab's sidebar renders the 9 entries in the two groups listed above.
- [ ] Confirm the Chain Operators tab opens on Guides > Getting started (the plan-sanctioned interim state described above).
- [ ] Group-name call: the first group inside the tab is named "Get started" (the plan names the tab but not its first group; this matches the skeleton convention slices 3-5 will use). Say the word if you prefer "Welcome" or "Introduction"; it is a one-string change.
- [ ] Merge when satisfied, then confirm ethereum-optimism/solutions#987 closure stands (cross-repo closes do not auto-fire).
